collection.description: The girl says their family was travelling along the far coast when the river rose in the night, and in the dark she lost them.

ask.text:
Two small children have walked out of the jungle into the village, holding hands: a girl of about six and a baby brother she is carrying on her hip, both scratched and filthy and very hungry. The girl says their family was travelling along the far coast when the river rose in the night, and in the dark she lost them. She has been walking for three days.
She has walked straight up to (subject), out of everyone in the village, and is holding up the baby. "Can you hold him?" she says. "My arms are tired."
Should (subject) take the children in, or organise a search for the family first?

c1o1.text: Nobody ever comes looking. The village sends canoes along the coast, and finds the family's camp washed away and empty. The girl and her brother stay with (subject). The girl is very serious and very helpful and doesn't laugh for a long time. When she does, at last, at something silly (subject) does with a spoon, (subject) does it again, and again, every day after that.

c1o2.text: A week later a man and a woman come stumbling along the beach, calling the children's names. The reunion is so loud the whole village comes out. The parents won't let go of the children for a day. Then they decide they have had enough of travelling, and {#made:only one of them can stay, as the village has no room for more|only two of them can stay, as the village has no room for more|the four of them stay}, and the girl still follows (subject) everywhere.

c1.text: (subject) takes the baby, who is heavy and asleep, and takes the girl's hand, and walks them both to (subject.his/her) hut. The girl eats three bowls of stew without stopping...

c2o1.text: On the second day, they find the family on a sandbank in the river mouth, cold, hungry and frantic: a mother, a father and an older son with a broken arm. The canoes bring them home. When the girl sees them, she screams so loudly the birds go up off the whole island. {#made:Only one of them can stay; the village has no room for more|Only two of them can stay; the village has no room for more|They stay}.

c2o2.text: They find only the empty camp, washed out by the river, and nobody in it. The girl doesn't cry when (subject) tells her. She just nods, as if she knew. She stays in the village, and (healer), who has milk to spare, takes the baby. The girl visits her brother every day.

c2.text: (subject) hands the children to the healers and gets the fishers together. They set off along the coast with canoes and torches, calling...
